doc.title: Don Albert and Herbert Hall Interview, 1978-08-03

title: Robichaux family and Tanglefoot
summary: The Robichaux bandleaders John and Joe, the trumpeter Mutt, and a garbled nickname passage.

story.theme_name: Who was in the band: naming sidemen and personnel
story.community_name: Who played in the band: reciting personnel

blocks.x: Oh, who was Tanglefoot? You were talking about how they call it?
How you call it? Tanglefoot? Oh, yeah.
I see. I haven't got nothing mixed up. I don't know if you meant Joe or John. Mm-hmm. Well, John was all right.

Tanglefoot is simple. That's what I'm like. Pigeon Joe is one. Mm-hmm. That's what I'm saying. Yeah. Yeah. Yeah, boy. Look at this nippy. He's a great dad. But I know when people talk about Robichaud today, very often they mean the old man, John, the left-handed bomb. Yeah. Even though Joe had quite a reputation with his family. Yeah.
And they still say John Robichaud. And they talk about Robichaud.
Yeah, but John never meant too big. Yeah.
He went up north and made records.
But it didn't click. I don't know why, either.
Not that it was a bad band. Yeah. Did you listen to the trumpet player ever with old man Robichaud?
Yeah. I was. Mutt. Oh, was Mutt with him? I didn't think so.
Mm-hmm. But that's before my time. Yeah.
He said, he was one of those. And I said, that old Fred Kessler here, and he's a little old man. And how old were you then? Good boy. Good boy.
Good boy. Did you ever play with Mutt? I'm pretty.
